prompt: In many countries, services that were once run by the state, such as prisons, railways and rubbish collection, are now operated by private companies under government contracts. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
Whether a public service should be run by a private contractor depends less on ownership than on a practical question: can the government describe what it wants precisely enough to buy it? Where it can, contracting out is usually an improvement. The difficulty is that in many countries the practice has spread well beyond such services, and for that reason I consider the development, on balance, a negative one.

The case for it is strongest where quality is visible. A council that contracts out rubbish collection can specify the streets, the days and the standard of cleanliness, check each of them weekly, and replace a contractor that falls short. Under those conditions a private firm has every reason to find cheaper vehicles, better routes and fewer missed collections, and the public benefits from an ingenuity that a department with no competitor is seldom required to show. Cleaning, catering and routine maintenance share these features, and outsourcing them tends to work.

A prison shares none of them. What matters most there — whether inmates leave less likely to offend, whether staff can calm a confrontation before it turns violent — is hard to measure and becomes apparent only over years. A contract must therefore reward what can be counted instead, such as escapes, occupancy and cost per place, and a company paid on those terms will quite rationally deliver them while economising on everything else. Railways add a further difficulty: so few firms are capable of running one that a failing operator cannot credibly be dismissed, and a contractor that knows it cannot be replaced is under little more pressure than the ministry it succeeded. In both cases the state keeps the responsibility and gives up the control.

The development is therefore positive where a service can be specified and competed for, and negative where it cannot, and it is into the second kind that the practice has been spreading. A government that keeps prisons, and any other service whose value lies in judgement rather than measurable output, under its own management sacrifices little efficiency and retains the ability to put right what goes wrong.
title: Private companies running public services
